record_type_quote:
In a previous study, deception was accurately detected
in at least 90% of the participants in two independent cohorts. This study attempted to replicate those findings using a
different scanner and location.

targets.authors: Kozel, F. A.; Revell, L. J.; Lorberbaum, J. P.; Shastri, A.; Elhai, J. D.; Horner, M. D.; Smith, A.; Nahas, Z.; Bohning, D. E.; George, M. S.
targets.title: A pilot study of functional magnetic resonance imaging brain correlates of deception in healthy young men.
targets.evidence_quote:
The Lie-minus-True group map revealed significant
activation in similar regions from the prior cohorts using this
paradigm (see Figure and Table). Specifically, the regions of
right orbitofrontal, right inferior frontal, right middle frontal,
and right cingulate gyrus have replicated now in five
independent groups from four studies across several
paradigms [3-5].
targets.outcome_quote:
This method for detecting deception was successfully
replicated on a different scanner at a different location for
both the individual and group analyses.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The explicit overall verdict states successful replication for both group and individual analyses. It covers the group-level findings attributed to references 3–5, outweighing the specific left temporal contrast.

reasoning: PDF title and seven authors match the assignment; the publisher abstract page has a malformed expanded author list, resolved using the PDF byline. New participants test the 2005 individual diagnostic finding and group activation findings explicitly attributed to all three original papers in references 3–5. These are independently retested group findings, rather than including earlier papers solely because they precede the 2005 paper in a chain. Reference 30 is a comparison with another experiment, not a finding retested here. The two cohorts in the 2005 paper remain one paper-level target. No target DOIs are printed.
